# Template Index and Section Maps

How the spec templates map to artifacts, what sections each template contains, and the conventions for replacing placeholders. The template files in the package's `templates/` directory are the source of truth for exact structure; this index tells you which template renders which artifact, the section order to fill, and how to substitute values.

## Template → Artifact Map

| Template file | Renders | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `templates/README.md.template` | `README.md` | Front door; includes the executive summary. |
| `templates/spec.md.template` | `[featureName].spec.md` | Always rendered. |
| `templates/plan.md.template` | `[featureName].plan.md` | Cursor plan format (YAML frontmatter + body). |
| *(story package)* | `[featureName].story.md` | Generated by **{{skill:story.story-authoring}}** (`mode: create`) — **skipped** when the story source is external (Jira issue or external file). The story template and authoring live in the **story** package, not here. |

There is no story template in this package — the story is produced by the story package. There is no summary template — the executive summary is a section of the README template. There is no review template here; the review artifact's shape is defined by the review rubric, not by a `templates/` file.

## Section Maps

Fill every section the template defines. Lists below give the section order so nothing is dropped; consult the template file for the exact headings and placeholder names.

### README.md

1. Overview (+ note that the README absorbs the executive summary)
2. Executive Summary — status/version/created line; What Gets Implemented; Core Approach; Key Files; Testing Strategy (at a glance)
3. Documents — index linking each sibling artifact (story is conditional on story source)
4. Quick Reference — What This Provides; What This Doesn't Provide (out of scope)
5. Architecture Summary (diagram)
6. User Experience (example usage)
7. Key Concepts
8. Implementation Overview — Timeline; Dependencies
9. Quality Standards — Testing; Documentation; Code Quality
10. Safety Guarantees
11. Performance Targets
12. Getting Started — For Implementers; For Reviewers
13. Status (table)
14. Related Documents
15. Success Criteria

### [featureName].story.md

1. Header — feature name, branch, created date, status, original description
2. User Scenarios & Testing — prioritized user stories (P1/P2/P3) with acceptance scenarios; Edge Cases
3. Requirements — Functional (FR-###); Non-Functional (NFR-###); Key Entities
4. Success Criteria — Measurable Outcomes (SC-###)
5. Technical Approach (optional, high-level only)
6. Dependencies & Constraints
7. Security & Privacy Considerations
8. Out of Scope
9. Future Enhancements (optional)
10. Open Questions
11. Stakeholders & Reviewers
12. References & Resources (optional)

Content standards and the template for this artifact live in the **story package** (`{{skill:story.story-authoring}}`). Keep it technology-agnostic. The section list above is retained here only so spec readers know the story's shape.

### [featureName].spec.md

1. Header — Story link (conditional on story source); created date; status
2. Overview
3. Architecture — High-Level; Component Design; Data Flow
4. Algorithms & Logic
5. Data Model — Data Structures; Database Schema (if applicable)
6. API Design — Endpoints (if applicable); Function Signatures
7. Technical Decisions
8. File Structure — New Files; Files to Modify
9. Implementation Details
10. Integration Points
11. Edge Cases & Error Handling
12. Security Considerations
13. Performance Considerations
14. Testing Strategy
15. Configuration
16. Deployment Considerations
17. Dependencies
18. Migration Path (if applicable)
19. Open Technical Questions
20. References

Content standards for this artifact live in the `technical-spec-authoring` skill. Code examples belong here, not in the story.

### [featureName].plan.md

YAML frontmatter: `name`, `overview`, `todos` (array of `{ id, content, status }`), `isProject: false`.

Body sections:

1. Status (table; links to spec and story)
2. How to Use This Plan
3. Technology Stack
4. Architecture Overview
5. Implementation Phases (3–7 phases; each references its `p{N}-*` todos)
6. Timeline Summary
7. Success Criteria
8. Risk Mitigation
9. Dependencies
10. Rollout Plan
11. Post-Implementation
12. Final Validation
13. Code Review Checklist
14. Sign-off
15. Quick Command Reference
16. Notes

The YAML schema, todo `id` convention (`p{N}-{slug}`), and status lifecycle are owned by the `spec-plan-format` skill. Load it before authoring or editing the plan; do not infer the format from this index.

## Placeholder-Replacement Conventions

The templates use Handlebars-style variables. Replace them as follows:

| Convention | Rule |
|---|---|
| Variable syntax | `{{variableName}}` — replace each with the resolved value. Leave **no** `{{…}}` markers in the finished artifact. |
| Feature name in prose/headings | Title Case (e.g., "User Authentication"). |
| Feature name in filenames and the directory | kebab-case (e.g., `user-authentication`). The `[featureName].X.md` files use the kebab-case form. |
| Dates | Use today's date for `{{created_date}}`. |
| Version | Default `{{version}}` to `1.0.0` unless specified. |
| Status | Default `{{status}}` to `Draft` for a new spec. |
| `<!-- ACTION REQUIRED -->` comments | These mark placeholder regions in the templates. Replace the placeholder content; remove the comment once the section is filled. |

## The External-Story Conditional

The story-gating conditional appears in `README.md.template`, `spec.md.template`, and `plan.md.template`:

```handlebars
{{#if storyPath}}
… external story branch: link to {{storyPath}} (external file or Jira issue), note "maintained externally" …
{{else}}
… local story branch: link to ./[featureName].story.md …
{{/if}}
```

- Render the **`{{else}}`** branch for a local story (no external source) — and generate `[featureName].story.md`.
- Render the **`{{#if storyPath}}`** branch for an external source (file path or Jira issue) — and skip the local story file.

Preserve this conditional verbatim when editing templates. It is the single switch that controls whether a local story is generated and which target every cross-reference points at. See the parent `SKILL.md` (Story Source section) for how to detect which branch applies from the story-source value.
